framework.name: JISC BDC Teacher Role Profile (Higher Education)
key_principles: This is one lens on the BDC framework, not a separate competency framework
No one will have all capabilities listed
The profile does not define levels of achievement natively
AI maturity level mapping is an interpretive overlay

Digital Teaching sub-element covers eight areas of digital teaching practice. Higher-level descriptors (Senior/Principal Fellow) align with AI maturity levels 4-5. Assessment and feedback particularly prominent. Profile maps to PSF 2023 dimensions.

cross_reference_frameworks.name: JISC AI Maturity Model for Education

digital_teaching_practice_areas: Planning and designing for digital LTA
Accessibility and universal design for learning

aspects.name: Digital Proficiency and Productivity
aspects.description: The ability to use digital devices, networks, applications, software and services. How you use digital skills to accomplish tasks effectively and productively.

sub_elements.name: Digital Proficiency
sub_elements.description: Ability to use digital devices, networks, applications, AI, software and services; confident adoption of new tools; capacity to deal with problems.

sub_elements.name: Digital Productivity
sub_elements.description: Using digital tools and services to carry out tasks effectively; choosing the right tools for each task including AI; adapting tools to personal needs.

aspects.name: Digital Creation, Problem-Solving and Innovation
aspects.description: Digital production of content, using digital evidence to solve problems and make decisions, and willingness to try new practices with digital technology including AI.

sub_elements.name: Digital Creation
sub_elements.description: Digital production of content including AI-generated content; understanding different digital production processes.

sub_elements.name: Digital Research and Problem-Solving
sub_elements.description: Using digital evidence including AI-generated evidence to solve problems, make decisions and answer questions.

sub_elements.name: Digital Innovation
sub_elements.description: Willingness to try new practices with digital technology including Generative AI; assessing benefits, risks and accessibility.

aspects.name: Digital Learning and Development
aspects.description: Learning in digital settings and through digital media. Includes digital teaching practices for those in teaching roles.

sub_elements.name: Digital Learning
sub_elements.description: Learning effectively in technology-rich environments; using digital networks for CPD; reflecting on digital practices.

sub_elements.name: Digital Teaching
sub_elements.description: Teaching effectively with digital tools and in digital environments. For Teacher profile, covers eight areas of digital teaching practice.

aspects.name: Information, Data and Media Literacies
aspects.description: Finding, evaluating, managing and sharing digital information, data and media content including AI-generated content.

sub_elements.name: Information Literacy
sub_elements.description: Finding, evaluating, managing and sharing information in digital environments.

sub_elements.name: Data Literacy
sub_elements.description: Understanding and working with data including collection, analysis, interpretation and visualisation.

sub_elements.name: Media Literacy
sub_elements.description: Critically reading, creating and evaluating media content including AI-generated media.

aspects.name: Digital Communication, Collaboration and Participation
aspects.description: Communicating effectively in digital media, collaborating in digital teams, and participating in digital communities.

sub_elements.name: Digital Communication
sub_elements.description: Communicating effectively in digital media and spaces; designing digital communications including using AI.

sub_elements.name: Digital Collaboration
sub_elements.description: Participating in digital teams using shared tools including AI-powered collaboration tools.

sub_elements.name: Digital Participation
sub_elements.description: Participating in digital communities, civic engagement and professional networks.

aspects.name: Digital Identity and Wellbeing
aspects.description: Managing professional digital identity and presence, and maintaining health and wellbeing in digital and AI-mediated environments.

sub_elements.name: Digital Identity Management
sub_elements.description: Building and managing professional digital identity, reputation and presence.

sub_elements.name: Digital Wellbeing
sub_elements.description: Managing health, safety, relationships and work-life balance in digital environments; using technology aligned with values.

progression_levels.name: Approaching and Understanding
progression_levels.description: Interest in AI; understanding impact on other sectors. No formal AI activity. Basic digital capabilities developing at individual level. At institutional level, digital activities are dispersed and project-based.
progression_levels.target: Foundational awareness of AI concepts and their relevance to role and organisation
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Develop understanding of what AI is, how it works at a basic level, and why it matters for education
progression_levels.data_maturity_expectation: L1 Reactive: No formal data management; embryonic processes; data not viewed as important

progression_levels.name: Experimenting and Exploring
progression_levels.description: Pilots within existing processes; data culture emerging; responsible AI processes established; initial AI guidance produced. Individuals actively experimenting with AI tools.
progression_levels.target: Active exploration of AI tools and responsible use habits within existing workflows
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Build practical skills through guided experimentation with AI tools relevant to role
progression_levels.data_maturity_expectation: L2 Working towards proactive: Nascent capability emerging; informal roles; some trust in key outputs

progression_levels.name: Operational
progression_levels.description: Institutional AI principles established; systemic staff AI skills/literacy approach; everyday AI used institution-wide; task-specific AI for one or more processes. Confident, routine AI-augmented practice.
progression_levels.target: Routine, informed AI-augmented practice integrated into professional workflows
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Demonstrate confident, systematic and responsible application of AI within professional domain
progression_levels.data_maturity_expectation: L3 Proactive: Data management embedded for key datasets; roles emerged; quality measurement patchy

progression_levels.name: Embedded
progression_levels.description: AI embedded in strategy (not standalone); data maturity allows AI consideration for all new systems; mature lifecycle management including procurement and continuous monitoring. Leading AI integration.
progression_levels.target: AI-enhanced practice as default; strategic use; mentoring others; contributing to institutional AI strategy
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Lead AI integration in professional domain; contribute to organisational AI strategy and governance
progression_levels.data_maturity_expectation: L4 Working towards integrated: Key organisational capability; most outputs automated; data governance formalised

progression_levels.name: Optimised/Transformed
progression_levels.description: AI supports delivery of learning optimising outcomes for all learners; right tasks automated freeing staff for creativity and human interaction. Sector leadership in AI innovation.
progression_levels.target: Innovative, transformative AI practice; optimised workflows; recognised leadership in AI application
progression_levels.overall_curricular_goal: Shape sector practices; innovate transformative AI-enabled approaches; champion ethical and inclusive AI adoption
progression_levels.data_maturity_expectation: L5 Integrated: Strategic capability; foundation for innovative services; predictive analytics; fully integrated
